name_note: GTDB divides Catenibacterium mitsuokai into more than one species; the genomes placed in mitsuoka_A carry the NCBI names Catenibacterium mitsuokai and Catenibacterium faecis.

sentences.text: Catenibacterium mitsuokai was proposed as the single species of the new genus Catenibacterium, for six Eubacterium-like strains from human faeces.
The strains belong to the Clostridium subphylum and have a specific phylogenetic association with Lactobacillus catenaformis and Lactobacillus vitulinus.
A metagenomic survey revealed an unknown bacterial clade within the species to be significantly more prevalent in non-urbanized populations compared to urbanized ones.
A strain of that clade, isolated from the stool of a healthy adult volunteer, is strictly anaerobic, appears as long chains of Gram-positive rods and produces acetate with glucose.
That isolate forms a distinct subspecies of C. mitsuokai, with average nucleotide identity lower than 94 percent to the previously described C. mitsuokai subsp. mitsuokai.
